questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(A) Uni-Factor Theory
(B) Theory of Primary Mental Abilities
(C) Theory of Multiple Intelligences
(D) Two-Factor Theory

List-II
(I) Howard Gardner
(II) Charles Spearman
(III) Alfred Binet
(IV) Louis Thurstone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
Alfred Binet conceptualized the Uni-Factor (One-Factor) theory of intelligence, positing a single general entity of common abilities.
